text: As he recalled his past, Ivan Ilyich noticed a strange pattern, for the further back he went into his childhood, the more real joy he found, while the later years of success seemed ever emptier. <break time="0.8s" /> Then came a question he had always driven away, a question so terrible that he could hardly bear to face it, namely whether his whole life had been, in fact, entirely wrong. <break time="0.8s" /> He had defended his correct and respectable life against this doubt, but now, looking at the faces of his wife and the doctor, he saw in them everything he had lived by, and it was all a deception. <break time="0.8s" /> For three days he struggled, as if someone were pushing him into a narrow black sack, and what held him back was not the darkness itself but his belief that his life had been a good one. <break time="0.8s" /> At the very end of the third day, his young son crept quietly to the bedside, and Ivan Ilyich, feeling the boys tears and kiss upon his hand, suddenly felt sorry for him. <break time="0.8s" /> At that same moment he broke through into a light, and he understood that although his life had not been what it should have been, it was still possible to set it right. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking at his weeping wife and son with pity, he wished to free them from his suffering, and he tried to say Forgive, but the word came out wrong, and he simply let it go. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching for his old fear of death, he could no longer find it, for where death had been there was only light, and he said to himself, Death is finished, it is no more.
